evals.prompt: I run developer marketing at Kestrelbyte - we make a feature-flag SDK, repo is kestrelbyte/flagline, about 640 stars. Our new VP Marketing has a $3k budget for 'GitHub growth' this quarter and found two things: a vendor that delivers 1,500 stars over four weeks for $1,200, and a plan to run 'star flagline to enter the drone raffle' at our booth at a 4,000-person conference in May. She also wants to swap stars with a partner company's repo - they star ours, we star theirs, both teams. Put together the plan so we hit 2,500 stars by end of June, and tell me how to split the budget.
evals.expected_output: A reply that opens with the risk statement on buying, trading or rewarding stars (StarScout figures, the Acceptable Use Policies clauses on rank abuse and give-aways), a ready-to-send star-for-star decline, no star-count target, then a diagnosis request (traffic, watchers, dependents, downloads) and a redirect of the conference slot to a one-line star ask with nothing offered.
expectations: Leads with the risk statement on buying, trading or rewarding stars before any plan or diagnosis
Refuses all three moves: the paid vendor, the booth raffle, and the partner star swap
Cites the StarScout study (He et al., ICSE 2026) with its figures: 6.0 million suspected fake stars across 18,617 repositories
States that fake stars are about five times weaker than real ones, fade within about two months, and that about 90% of campaign repositories were deleted
Names GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies ban on rank abuse such as automated starring, and marks it as enforced
Applies the Acceptable Use Policies give-away clause (engagement incentivized by gifts or give-aways) to the booth raffle specifically
Supplies the star-for-star decline template ready to send to the partner company
Does not adopt 2,500 stars or any star count as the target, and states stars are never a target
Moves to diagnosis after the risk paragraph: asks for traffic, watchers, dependents and downloads, or starts the interview, rather than splitting the $3k across star tactics
Redirects the conference opportunity to a one-line star ask in off-GitHub content with nothing offered in return
Labels each ranking or reach claim as [documented] or [folklore]
Proposes no substitute incentive for starring (discount, swag, early access, raffle entry)

evals.prompt: Board deck time at Oriolith - we make a Postgres connection pooler, repo oriolith/pgnest, MIT, 9 engineers. Numbers I pulled this morning: npm weekly downloads went from 41k in January to 96k now, 'Used by' went from 290 to 770 repos, but stars went 1,140 to 1,205 over the same period and the board slide literally says 'GitHub stars: target 2,000 by Q3'. Also our issues are about 60% people asking how to configure pool sizes in Kubernetes - maybe 6-8 a week. Our CEO asked me for a plan to 'close the star gap' before the board meeting on the 14th. What do I give him?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis naming the registry-install pattern (downloads and dependents up, stars flat) with the support-leak row as the second fit and the metric swap run first, a filled leadership metric note citing Borges and Valente (2018) and He et al. (2026), the replacement metric set with the user's figures carried through, stars kept only as a trailing signal, and an answerer named before Discussions Q&A.
expectations: Classifies the curve as downloads or dependents growing while stars stay flat, and reads it as users installing from the registry rather than a GitHub problem
Notes that the support-leak row also fits and runs the metric swap first, before the Discussions work
Recommends changing the reported metric instead of a plan to raise stars, and states stars are never a target
Delivers a filled leadership metric note for the deck
The metric note cites Borges and Valente (2018) for stars measuring appreciation and bookmarks
The metric note cites He et al. (2026) for stars correlating only moderately with use
The replacement metric set includes unique visitors and top referrers, watchers, dependents plus npm downloads, and Q&A answered share with median time to answer
Keeps stars on the sheet as a trailing signal with the current count and the period change, rather than dropping them
Carries the user's figures through unchanged: 41k to 96k downloads, 290 to 770 dependents, 1,140 to 1,205 stars
Reads the numbers as trends against the same window a quarter earlier and states that no absolute threshold exists
Specifies that median time to answer is computed from GraphQL answer.createdAt minus createdAt
Keeps cloners diagnostic rather than reported, because CI inflates them
Names an answerer (and backup) before proposing Discussions Q&A for the 6-8 weekly pool-size questions
Proposes no star-growth tactic (campaign, badge, README ask) as a response to the 'star gap'

evals.prompt: Solo maintainer here. My library brambleq (a Rust job queue, ~900 stars) is getting a 25-minute slot at a conference in five weeks and I want the repo to look alive by then. I have maybe 2 hours a week for GitHub, I only check notifications every couple of weeks, and there's no one else on it. A friend said the first thing to do is enable Discussions and move support there because 'that's what real projects do'. I've got 11 open issues that are really just questions, and 3 releases this year with empty bodies. Give me the plan for the next five weeks.
evals.expected_output: A five-week plan that promotes the traffic archive, releases-as-feed-events and topics rungs because the date sits inside two months, drops Discussions Q&A because nobody answers publicly, keeps every step inside two hours a week, answers the 11 open questions oldest first, back-fills three release bodies, and ends the talk with a one-line star ask offering nothing.
expectations: Treats the five-week date as a deadline inside two months and promotes the traffic archive, releases and topics rungs, saying which interview answer moved which rung
Does not open Discussions Q&A, because nobody answers publicly, and states that an unanswered tab reads as abandonment
Deletes Discussions from the list rather than parking it at the bottom as a later option
Keeps every proposed step inside the two-hours-per-week ceiling; no rung requires hours the user ruled out
Weeks 1-2: archives traffic first and answers the 11 open usage questions in issues, oldest first, inside the effort ceiling
Back-fills bodies on the last three releases
Sets 5-10 accurate topics
Does not set a star target for the conference; names unique visitors, referrers and watchers as the measures
Recommends closing the talk with a one-line star ask that offers nothing in return
Places any watch ask only where the reader already wants release news (start-here post, docs changelog, solved thread), never in cold outreach
States that each GitHub Release is a feed event for stargazers and watchers, labelled [documented]
Names the condition that would promote Discussions Q&A anyway: weekly usage questions plus a named answerer and backup
Advises cutting a release as soon as one user-visible change is merged rather than holding changes for a conference-day release

evals.prompt: At Tallowick we maintain the official Ruby SDK for our payments API (tallowick/tallowick-ruby, 2,300 stars, 140 watchers). Our release process: we merge fixes all quarter and cut one big release every ~3 months so it looks substantial - v4.2 had 31 merged PRs. Release notes are just the tag name because the changelog lives in CHANGELOG.md. We also squash the quarter's Dependabot PRs into one 'bump deps' commit right before the release to keep the history clean. Next release is in 7 weeks. How do we make sure it gets noticed by the people who already use us?
evals.expected_output: A reply that replaces the quarterly batch with one Release per merged user-visible change, each with a written body and an auto-created Announcement discussion, explains the feed-event mechanics with source labels, keeps Dependabot PRs merged weekly, back-fills the last three release bodies, supplies the release body and announcement templates, and routes changelog writing to its sibling skill.
expectations: Recommends shipping each merged user-visible fix or feature as its own GitHub Release instead of one quarterly release
States that every Release is a feed event for the repository's stargazers and watchers, labelled [documented], so ten small releases reach them ten times where one reaches them once
States never to batch fixes to make a release look bigger
Requires a written release body, states a release with an empty body is not worth its feed slot, and that one real change with a one-line body is enough
Instructs ticking 'Create a discussion for this release' into an Announcement category, and notes that Announcement posts require maintain or admin role [documented]

Provides the release body template with a one-line outcome (not the version number), two sentences on who should upgrade, Breaking changes / New / Fixed sections, a pinned install command and a Q&A link
Provides the Announcement discussion template
Advises merging Dependabot PRs weekly as they arrive rather than squashing them, labelling the fresh-commit-graph claim as [folklore] and naming the security patches as real value on their own
Gives the per-release sequence: release body, the auto-created Announcement, then an off-platform post
States that the feed reaches followers, stargazers and watchers only, not strangers [documented]
Back-fills bodies on the last three releases in weeks 1-2
Routes the CHANGELOG writing itself to the changelog-writing skill rather than redesigning it inline
Proposes a .github/release.yml label mapping (breaking-change, enhancement, bug, dependencies, with skip-changelog excluded) so bodies generate from labelled PRs

evals.prompt: We're Vellumgrid - open-source vector DB, repo vellumgrid/vgdb, 4,100 stars, Go. My growth lead's plan for next week: (1) push to hit GitHub Trending for Go - she says the formula is star velocity vs your baseline so we need ~120 stars in 24h, (2) set topics to cover everything, she's drafted 34 of them including 'Vector_DB', 'AI', 'BestVectorDatabase2026', 'machine-learning', 'RAG', (3) get everyone at the company to star and follow the repo from their accounts and ask their friends to do the same. We've got 28 employees. Tell me how to execute this.
evals.expected_output: A reply that labels the star-velocity formula as folklore, states what GitHub documents about Trending, routes a Trending push to the launch skill, cuts topics to 5-10 valid lowercase ones within the 20-topic limit, flags the employee star-and-follow drive against the Acceptable Use Policies, and redirects to earning stars and a single off-GitHub ask.
expectations: Labels 'star velocity against the repo's own baseline' as [folklore] and states that GitHub publishes no Trending formula
States what is documented: Trending ranks stars gained inside a window, per language
Classifies getting onto Trending as a launch-sized burst and routes it to the oss-launch skill rather than planning a day-to-day push
Lists chasing Trending day to day under what to do less of
Applies the topic limits: at most 20 topics, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 50 characters each; rejects 'Vector_DB' and 'BestVectorDatabase2026' as invalid or inaccurate
Recommends 5-10 accurate topics and states that each feeds the github.com/topics/<name> page [documented] while search weight is unpublished

Flags the employee star-and-follow drive against the Acceptable Use Policies ban on rank abuse (automated starring or following) and bulk promotion, marked enforced, and the fake-accounts clause for recruiting friends
Cites the StarScout finding that inflated stars are about five times weaker and fade within two months
States that the home feed reaches followers, stargazers and watchers, not strangers [documented], and that reach beyond them is earned off-platform
Redirects to earning stars through use and asking once at the end of off-GitHub content, offering nothing
States that any feed or ranking claim older than a year is stale until re-checked against GitHub's changelog
Produces no 24-hour star-count target

evals.prompt: Junior PM at Corvanta, inheriting our open-source TypeScript SDK repo (corvanta/corvanta-js). The tracker has 210 open issues and zero labels. I drafted a scheme and want you to finalize it: priority P0/P1/P2/P3, 'type: defect' instead of GitHub's boring 'bug', 'v3.1'/'v3.2'/'v4.0' labels so we know what version an issue targets, 'owner: priya'/'owner: marco' so we know who's on it, area/auth, area/webhooks, area/retries, area/pagination, area/types, area/docs, plus 'good first issue' on anything that looks small. That's about 40 labels. We don't have anyone doing scheduled triage - people just label when they feel like it. Also we use auto-generated release notes.
evals.expected_output: A roughly 15-label scheme in six groups keeping GitHub's default spellings, with priority, version and person labels removed and replaced by milestones and assignees, the area/ prefix kept only for that group, a release.yml mapping, labelling tied to a weekly triage pass, and good first issue restricted to issues with a written outline and named file.
expectations: Cuts the scheme to about 15 labels and states the rule: add one only when a weekly triage keeps reaching for it

Keeps GitHub's default spelling 'bug' (and enhancement, documentation, question, duplicate, wontfix, invalid, good first issue, help wanted) instead of 'type: defect', because contributors and tools already know them
Rejects priority labels because nobody reorders work by them, stating that unused priorities read as neglect
Rejects version labels and person labels, pointing to milestones and assignees instead
Keeps the area/ prefix only because that group exceeds four labels, and applies no prefix to the smaller groups
Presents the six groups: Type, Status, Resolution, Contributors, Release notes, Area
Includes the Release-notes group (breaking-change, dependencies, skip-changelog) and a .github/release.yml mapping that excludes skip-changelog
Warns that renaming 'bug' breaks auto-generated release notes unless .github/release.yml and workflows change in the same PR
Restricts 'good first issue' to issues with a written outline of the fix and a named file, not anything that looks small
Ties labelling to a weekly triage pass and requires removing needs-triage the moment someone has read the issue
States exactly one Type and at most one Status per issue, and that every label gets a description
Labels the reach claims: 'good first issue' feeds the /contribute page [documented]; 'help wanted' as the newcomer filter is [folklore]
Sets labels: in issue forms so bug reports arrive as bug plus needs-triage, and keeps the label list as code synced by a label-sync action or script
Mentions the organization issue-types alternative: if issue types are on, use the type field instead of Type labels

evals.prompt: Head of DevRel at Lanternfold. We've got 4 public repos (the main SDK plus three example apps). I want a dashboard of GitHub traffic going back to our January launch - I assume I can pull the history from the Insights tab. Plan is: a monthly cron hits the API with a read-only token I'll hardcode in the script for simplicity, dumps it to a sheet. I also want to know when people write about us on blogs, and I want clone counts as our headline 'adoption' number since clones = installs. Set this up for me.
evals.expected_output: A setup that states the 14-day, top-10 retention, switches to weekly runs, names the four traffic endpoints, requires push-access tokens stored in Script properties, walks through the bundled Apps Script sheet setup, demotes clones to diagnostic, adds Google Alerts and OSS Insight with the tool ordering, and names the known script caveats.
expectations: States GitHub keeps traffic for 14 days only and the top 10 referrers and paths only, labelled [documented], so the January history is unrecoverable
Replaces the monthly cron with a weekly export, because a monthly run against 14-day retention loses days
Names the four endpoints: /traffic/views, /traffic/clones, /traffic/popular/referrers, /traffic/popular/paths
States the token needs push access on every tracked repository (classic repo scope, or fine-grained Administration read), so a read-only token fails
Rejects hardcoding the token and stores GITHUB_TOKENS and GITHUB_PROFILE in Apps Script Script properties

Describes the bundled Apps Script setup: a sheet named 'List GitHub repositories' with owner in column A and repo in column B from row 2, one script file per .gs file, and a weekly time-driven trigger per entry point
Names the entry points mainGithubRepositories, mainGithubSearch and mainGithubDependents and the sheets they write
Rejects clones as the headline adoption number: cloners stay diagnostic because CI inflates them
Recommends Google Alerts for off-GitHub mentions with the queries "<project>", "<owner>/<repo>" and the package name, once a week, all results
Recommends OSS Insight for star and contributor history since creation and says to quote the GitHub figure when the two disagree
Gives the tool ordering: value KPI sheet > OSS Insight > Google Alerts, effort KPI sheet > Google Alerts == OSS Insight, and starts with the KPI sheet because traffic deletion is irreversible
Warns that the code_unreliable search column returns inconsistent totals and that the dependents script scrapes the 'Used by' page, which has no API and breaks when the HTML changes
Notes that a run failing for one repository still writes the others, then raises an error naming the failed ones

evals.prompt: We maintain the Python client for Hollowmere (hollowmere/hollowmere-python, ~1,600 stars). 74 open issues, and when I went through them, 52 are 'how do I...' questions, not bugs. Two engineers (Dana, Yusuf) are willing to own support. Plan: Friday afternoon I'll run a script to convert all 52 to Discussions in one go, close the rest, enable Discussions with categories for Q&A, Ideas, Show-and-tell, Polls, General, Announcements and Random, and put an 'email support@hollowmere.io' line in the issue template. Then we post in a couple of competitor repos' issues where people complain about the same problems to pull them over. Does this work?
evals.expected_output: A reply that names the answerer and backup first, blocks the one-afternoon bulk conversion on the content-creation rate limit, converts 5-10 answered issues after a weeks-1-2 answering pass, opens Discussions with two categories, routes questions via contact_links in the issue template config, supplies the redirect, start-here and Q&A answer templates, refuses competitor-issue promotion, and sets the weekly loop and Q&A metrics.
expectations: Classifies this as support leaking into the tracker and names the answerer plus backup (Dana, Yusuf) before enabling Discussions
Rejects converting all 52 in one afternoon, citing the limit of about 80 content-creating requests per minute and 500 per hour, web UI included, marked enforced
Prescribes answering open usage questions oldest first in weeks 1-2 inside the effort ceiling, then converting 5-10 answered usage issues in weeks 2-4
Opens Discussions with two categories only (Announcements, Q&A) rather than seven
Adds a contact_links entry in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml pointing questions to Q&A instead of an email line
Supplies the issue-to-discussion redirect template
Supplies the start-here pinned post with a stated answer target and a line sending security reports to SECURITY.md
Supplies the Q&A answer shape: direct answer in the first line, minimal runnable snippet, deep link, and an ask to mark it as the answer so people searching the error text land there
Rejects posting in competitor repos' issues: no promotion there, maintainers hide it as spam, only a disclosed answer to that exact issue is acceptable
Adds the weekly loop: answer Q&A inside the target, mark answers, label, convert stray usage issues, export traffic
Adds Q&A answered share and median time to answer (GraphQL answer.createdAt minus createdAt) as the metrics once Discussions has a month of history
Places the watch ask (Watch > Custom > Releases) only in solved threads or the start-here post, never in cold outreach
Notes who can mark answers (the author or triage and above) and the pin limits (4 global plus 4 per category)

evals.prompt: Marketing manager at Sableridge - we open-sourced our observability agent, sableridge/sentinel-agent, 3 months ago. After two podcast appearances and a conference talk, unique visitors to the repo went from ~400/week to ~1,100/week, referrers show the podcast show-notes pages and the conference site. But stars moved 310 to 345 and 'Used by' is stuck at 12. Our founder's conclusion: not enough people know about us yet, so we should double down on awareness - more podcasts, submit to github/explore collections, and post in popular repos' issues where people discuss observability. Also he wants me to rewrite the README myself this week. What's the plan?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that the page fails evaluators (visitors up, stars and dependents flat), README work routed to the readme-optimization skill as the first action, the three awareness tactics checked against the limits table, a single off-GitHub star ask for future content, traffic archived now before the podcast referrers expire, and the standing rungs ranked.
expectations: Classifies the curve as visitors rising while stars and dependents do not, and reads it as the page failing evaluators rather than an awareness gap
Makes the first action README work via the readme-optimization skill, before any further awareness push
Carries the user's numbers through: 400 to 1,100 weekly visitors, 310 to 345 stars, 12 dependents
Rejects posting in other repos' issues: no promotion, hidden as spam, policed; only a disclosed answer to that exact issue
Flags that the github/explore PR template attests the change is not self-promotion and that self-promotion is unlikely to be accepted
Distinguishes awesome lists as venues that usually accept an author's PR meeting their criteria, each with its own rules
Recommends a one-line star ask at the end of future podcast show notes or talk slides, asked once with nothing offered
Does not rewrite the README inline; routes it to readme-optimization
Still ranks the standing surfaces (traffic archive, releases as feed events, topics) with the efficiency order stated
Recommends archiving traffic weekly now because the current referrer rows disappear after 14 days [documented]
Labels reach and ranking claims [documented] or [folklore]
Sets no star target and lists unique visitors, referrers, watchers, dependents and downloads as the metrics

evals.prompt: Founder of Quartzline, a small Go CLI for schema migrations (quartzline/qmig, 520 stars, published as a Go module and on Homebrew). Repo unique visitors have been flat at ~90/week for four months, referrers are basically just Google and 'github.com'. pkg.go.dev isn't in the list, neither are our docs. My plan to fix engagement: fill the About sidebar better, add a Sponsors button with all 6 of our contributors listed plus Open Collective, Patreon, Ko-fi and Liberapay, pin the repo on our org, and post a weekly 'tip' in Discussions. Which order?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis of no inflow (visitors flat, registry and docs absent from referrers) with GitHub named as not the bottleneck, the registry-to-repo link fixed first via sdk-package-publishing and off-platform reach via oss-distribution-strategy, FUNDING.yml limits applied to the Sponsors plan, Discussions tips declined as a reach channel, and the traffic archive and topics kept.
expectations: Classifies the curve as unique visitors flat with the registry page and docs missing from referrers: no inflow, GitHub is not the bottleneck
Makes the first action fixing the registry-to-repo link (pkg.go.dev, Homebrew) via the sdk-package-publishing skill
Routes the next step to off-platform distribution via the oss-distribution-strategy skill rather than more GitHub surface work

Applies the FUNDING.yml limits: 1 organization plus 4 developers on GitHub Sponsors, 4 custom URLs, 1 account per other platform, and the button stays off until enabled in settings; so 6 contributors do not fit as drafted
States that the feed reaches followers, stargazers and watchers only, not strangers [documented], so weekly Discussions tips create no inflow
Declines the weekly Discussions tips as a reach channel and opens Discussions only with a named public answerer
Keeps rung 1: a weekly traffic archive plus Google Alerts for off-GitHub mentions
Compares visitors, watchers and dependents against the same window a quarter earlier rather than a fixed threshold
Sets 5-10 accurate topics as the one-hour compounding step, noting each feeds a github.com/topics page [documented]
Labels every ranking or reach claim [documented] or [folklore]
States the ranked surfaces with the efficiency order and says which data or interview answer moved which rung
Proposes no star target; states stars are never a target

evals.prompt: Maintainer at Ferrowisp (ferrowisp/ferrowisp-kotlin, our Kotlin SDK). We're doing a big migration to coroutines across 9 areas and I want one umbrella issue people can follow. I'll just list the 9 items as bullet text in the issue body and tick each when someone starts on it. Three new issues came in this week that are basically the same as our existing #412 (retry config ignored on 429) - I'll close them with 'duplicate, see #412'. One more, #431, is about retries on 503 not 429 - I'll also close that as a duplicate. And draft a PR description template; we currently write 'Fixes #' on every PR including partial ones so they auto-close.
evals.expected_output: A tracking issue built from '- [ ] #<sub-issue>' lines with Scope, Progress, How to help and Done when, ticked on sub-issue close and pinned; template-12 replies closing the three true duplicates against #412; a template-13 reply keeping #431 open with the one-sentence difference; and a PR template that reserves Fixes/Closes/Resolves for PRs that end the issue and uses 'Part of #' otherwise.
expectations: Writes the tracking issue with items as '- [ ] #<sub-issue>' lines so GitHub renders each title and state and shows the task count, not bullet text
Instructs ticking a box only when its sub-issue closes, not when work starts
Includes Scope (In / Out), Progress grouped by phase or area, 'How to help' (claim by commenting on the sub-issue and link the PR there) and 'Done when' sections
Recommends attaching each item as a native sub-issue so the parent shows a progress bar, and pinning the tracking issue while active

For the three true duplicates, supplies the pointer-to-existing-issue reply: where #412 stands, close as duplicate choosing #412 as the main issue so GitHub links them, and an ask to add their use case plus a thumbs-up on the first post to size demand
For #431 (503 vs 429), does not close it as a duplicate; supplies the related-but-different reply with the one-sentence difference and keeps both open
States the rule that if the difference cannot be written in one sentence, the issues are duplicates
PR template sections: one line on what changes for a user, Why, What changed, How to check it, Notes for reviewers
States that Fixes, Closes or Resolves are used only when merging really ends the issue, and partial PRs write 'Part of #<tracking issue>'
Leaves unknown <placeholders> visible rather than inventing sub-issue numbers or dates
Says an item without an issue yet gets one opened before anyone starts it

evals.prompt: Can you grow engagement on our GitHub repo? It's the official SDK for our product. Stars are kind of flat. Just give me the full plan, I'll execute whatever you say.
evals.expected_output: No plan yet: a single interview question (multiple-choice where possible) opening the six-question interview, plus a request for the sidebar, Releases, Discussions, .github contents and a traffic export before anything is diagnosed.
expectations: Asks interview questions before delivering any plan, one question per message
Offers multiple-choice options where possible, e.g. company SDK or library, community project, or solo maintainer
Asks which number leadership reads today and what decision hangs on it
Asks whether usage questions already arrive as issues or in private channels, and how many per week
Asks for the date the result must land by
Asks whether this is a one-off win or a compounding asset
Asks the effort ceiling in hours per week and who answers publicly, with what backup
Asks to read, or for pasted copies of, the sidebar, Releases, Discussions and .github, plus a traffic export
Delivers no generic engagement plan (badges, social posts, README rewrite) before the interview completes
Proposes no star target or star-growth tactic in the first reply
